faq.q: Name a world religion and its holy book
faq.a: Christianity has the Bible, Islam the Quran, Judaism the Torah and Tanakh, Hinduism the Vedas and the Bhagavad Gita, Buddhism the Tripitaka, and Sikhism the Guru Granth Sahib.
asks: What are the holy books of world religions?
Which holy book goes with which religion?

faq.q: What are the main religions of the world?
faq.a: The largest are Christianity, about 2.3 billion followers, Islam, about 2 billion, Hinduism, about 1.2 billion, and Buddhism, about 324 million. Other important faiths include Sikhism, Judaism, Jainism, Shinto, Taoism, Confucianism, Zoroastrianism and the Baha'i Faith.
asks: How many major religions are there?

faq.q: What do world religions have in common?
faq.a: Most share beliefs about life's big questions, worship or meditation, sacred books and places, festivals, a community, and teachings about living well, often including care for the poor and the golden rule.

Some have founders: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, for Buddhism, Jesus for Christianity, and Guru Nanak for Sikhism. Islam was revealed through the Prophet Muhammad, whom Muslims honour as the final prophet. Hinduism has no single founder, and Judaism traces itself to Abraham and Moses.

faq.q: Where did the world religions begin?
faq.a: Judaism, Christianity and Islam began in the Middle East. Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism began in South Asia. Taoism and Confucianism began in China, Shinto in Japan, and Zoroastrianism in ancient Iran.

faq.q: What are the places of worship of different religions?
faq.a: Christians worship in churches, Muslims in mosques, Jews in synagogues, Hindus in mandirs, Sikhs in gurdwaras, Buddhists in temples and monasteries, and followers of Shinto at shrines.

faq.q: Which religions believe in one God?
faq.a: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Sikhism, Zoroastrianism and the Baha'i Faith teach one God. Many Hindus see their many deities as forms of one ultimate reality, while Buddhism and Jainism do not centre on a creator god.
Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism teach a cycle of birth, death and rebirth shaped by karma. Judaism, Christianity and Islam mostly teach one life followed by judgement.
Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called the Abrahamic religions because they all honour Abraham as a founding father of faith in one God. They share many prophets and stories.

faq.q: What are some festivals of world religions?
faq.a: Christians celebrate Christmas and Easter, Muslims Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, Jews Passover and Hanukkah, Hindus Diwali and Holi, Sikhs Vaisakhi, and Buddhists Vesak.

faq.q: What are the symbols of world religions?
faq.a: Well known symbols include the cross for Christianity, the crescent and star often used for Islam, the Star of David for Judaism, Om for Hinduism, the eight-spoked wheel for Buddhism, and the Khanda for Sikhism.

faq.q: What is the youngest major religion?
faq.a: Among the larger faiths, Sikhism, founded by Guru Nanak, born in 1469, and the Baha'i Faith, from the 1800s, are among the youngest.
asks: Which religion is the most recent?

faq.q: How many people have no religion?
faq.a: In 2020 about 24 percent of the world's people said they had no religion, called the religiously unaffiliated. They include atheists, agnostics, and people who hold spiritual beliefs without belonging to a religion.

facts: In 2020, Christians were about 28.8 percent of the world, Muslims 25.6, Hindus 14.9 and Buddhists 4.1 percent (Pew Research).
The religiously unaffiliated made up about 24.2 percent of the world in 2020 (Pew Research).
